📚 Media Literacy

Learn simple ways to identify misinformation before sharing information online.

🔍 1. Identify Fake News

Look carefully at the headline. Extremely shocking, emotional or unbelievable headlines should be checked before being shared.

🌐 2. Check the Source

Check who published the information. Look for a known organisation, author, contact information and a trustworthy website.

✅ 3. Verify Information

Compare the claim with multiple reliable sources. Do not depend on only one social media post.

🚨 4. Identify Clickbait

Clickbait often uses exaggerated language, shocking claims and incomplete information to attract clicks.

🖼️ 5. Check Images and Videos

Images and videos can be edited or taken out of context. Check where the image originally appeared and when it was created.

📢 6. Don't Forward Unverified News

Forwarding unverified information can spread misinformation. Verify first and share later.

🔐 7. Social Media Safety

Avoid sharing personal information, passwords, OTPs and sensitive details with unknown people or websites.

🧠 8. Think Before You Share

Ask yourself: Who created this? What evidence is provided? Can I confirm this information somewhere else?
